title: Targeted Absolute Transcript Quantification in Single Cells After Whole Transcriptome Amplification
author: Franziska Durst
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.389grz6
materials: Single cells are manually isolated with a micromanipulator (Eppendorf, PatchMan NP2) as previously described (Hartmann CH, Klein CA. Nucleic Acids Res. 2006;34(21):e143). Isolated cells were picked in 1 µl of 1× PBS and transferred into 4.4 µl of lysing buffer containing 4 µl mTRAP™ Lysis Buffer (Active Motif) and 0.4 µl (10 ng) tRNA from E. coli MRE 600 (Roche). Picked cells suspended in the lysis can be stored at -80°C until further processing.

All pipetting steps are performed on ice in the sterile bench. For the preparation of the master mix, prepare enough for the WTA samples plus an additional spare volume. Primary or re-amplified WTA product was diluted five times with water and used as template in each test PCR (1 µl per sample) Prepare mastermix: ReagentFor one sample 10× PCR buffer1.0 µl Forward primer (8 µM)0.5 µl Reverse primer (8 µM)0.5 µl BSA (10 mg/ml)0.25 µl PANScript DNA Polymerase (5 U/µl)0.1 µl PCR-H2O6.65 µl Add figure legend here (optional) Place 9 μl of master mix in a 0.2 ml reaction tube per each sample Add 1 μl of template (five times diluted cDNA from single or small number of cells) Briefly vortex all batches, centrifuge and transfer to a thermocycler. The amplification in the thermocycler takes place according to the following program: TemperatureTime (h:min:sec)Cycles Step 195.0 °C00:04:00 Step 295.0 °C00:00:3042 cycles Step 3TA00:00:30 Step 472.0 °C00:01:30 Step 572.0 °C00:07:00 Step 64.0 °Cforever

Preparation of samples: The samples will be first diluted using PCR-H 2 O at a final concentration of 1 ng/µl. Preparation of qPCR Mastermix (MM): Table 1 shows the compositions of the mastermix. Prepare the respective amount for your samples. Attention: SyBr Green is light sensitive. Avoid working in the light! Pipette the qPCR plate: Distribute 15 µl of the MM per well of the 96-well plate using the multipipette. Add 5 µl of the diluted sample to the MM. As negative control, use PCR-H 2 O instead of cDNA (NTC). As a standard, use a calibrator DNA (Cal). All samples should be measured in triplicates. Seal the plate using a transparent foil. Vortex the plate, centrifuge shortly to spin the liquids down. Place the plate into the Cycler (here: LightCycler, Roche). Use the following program: Analysis of generated data Quality check and data export using Light Cycler Software NTC: Negative control should be negative. Melting curves of samples: Check whether only the desired amplicon was generated. Exclude samples showing multiple or unspecific peaks. Absolute quantification: Check whether amplification shows a sigmoid curve. Export Cp values and analyze them. Samples with average Cp-values >33 are considered as negative.

steps.title: Prepare PNA Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the PNA mix before thawing samples.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 19 μl lysis buffer and 1 μl protease solution.
Create a master mix containing equal volumes of lysis buffer/protease and PNAs (n μl lysis buffer/protease 1:20 + n μl PNA), where n is the number of samples.

steps.title: Sample Lysis and Bead Binding
steps.instruction: Perform lysis and bind targets to streptavidin beads.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve samples from the -80 °C cabinet.
Add 2 μl of prepared PNA mix to each sample (add to the upper fluid level without complete immersion, or add to the margin and centrifuge briefly).
Run the 'Lysis' cycler program (volume: 10 μl).
Resuspend streptavidin beads and add 4 μl of beads per tube.
Place all tubes in a 50 ml tube, secure with paper towels, and roll for 45 min at room temperature (RT).

steps.title: Prepare for RNA Isolation
steps.instruction: Set up equipment and reagents for the isolation process.

substeps.instruction: Preheat the hybridization oven and glass tubes to 44 °C.
Thaw washing buffer and cDNA synthesis reagents.
Prepare and label Axygen tubes for supernatants, each containing a 0.8 μl polyacrylamide carrier (PAA carrier).
Prepare and label a new set of Axygen tubes for the Tween wash step.
Prepare cDNA synthesis mix I and II; store on ice (prepare Mix II without enzyme, adding the enzyme shortly before use).

steps.title: Isolate RNA/gDNA
steps.instruction: Recover genomic DNA (gDNA) from supernatants using magnetic beads, ensuring beads do not dry out.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes briefly.
Add 10 μl of cDNA washing buffer + Igepal per tube and resuspend without creating air bubbles.
Place in magnet rack until beads are immobilized; carefully collect supernatants into the tubes with PAA carriers.
Resuspend beads in 20 μl cDNA washing buffer + Tween without air bubbles and transfer to a new tube.
Place in magnet rack until beads are immobilized; carefully collect supernatants.
Resuspend beads in 20 μl of cDNA washing buffer + Igepal without air bubbles.
Place in magnet rack until beads are immobilized; remove and collect supernatants twice to ensure no washing buffer residue remains.

steps.title: Prepare Primary WTA PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare the master mix and reactions for primary Whole Transcriptome Amplification (WTA).

substeps.instruction: Prepare Primer-Mix: 8 µl of each of the 6 primers (100 µM stock) + 152 µl PCR-H2O.
Perform all pipetting on ice in a sterile bench.
Prepare a master mix sufficient for WTA samples, a 3-fold positive control, a negative control (PCR water), and spare volume.
Dispense 49 μl of master mix into 0.2 ml reaction tubes per sample.
Add 1 μl of template (cDNA from single or small number of cells) or control.
Briefly vortex, centrifuge, and transfer to a thermocycler for amplification.

steps.title: Prepare Re-amplified WTA PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare reactions for re-amplification of WTA samples.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a master mix (as described for primary WTA).
Dispense 9.5 μl of master mix into 0.2 ml reaction tubes per sample.
Add 0.5 μl of template or control.
Centrifuge briefly and transfer to a thermocycler.

Alternatively, for a different re-amp version: place 9 μl of master mix in a 0.2 ml vessel and add 1 μl of a 1:5 dilution of the re-amplified WTA sample or control; centrifuge and amplify using the primary WTA program.

steps.title: Purify WTA DNA
steps.instruction: Purify the primary or re-amplified WTA using QIAquick columns.

substeps.instruction: If purifying only a portion, transfer the desired volume to a 0.2 ml tube; if purifying >40 μl, use 1.5 ml tubes.
If using PE buffer for the first time, add ethanol (96-100%) as indicated on the bottle.
Set centrifuge to 17,900 x g (13,000 rpm).
Add 5 volumes of PB buffer to each sample (e.g., 100 μl PB for 20 μl sample).
Mix by pipetting until no streaks are visible.
Apply sample to QIAquick column and centrifuge for 60 sec at 17,900 x g; discard flow-through.
Add 750 μL of PE buffer, centrifuge for 60 sec at 17,900 x g, and discard flow-through.
Centrifuge again for 60 sec at 17,900 x g to remove residual buffer.
Place column in a clean 1.5 ml tube; pipette PCR-H2O directly onto the filter (minimum 10 μl; recommended ≥20 μl for Reamps).
Incubate columns for 5-10 min at RT.
Centrifuge for 30 sec at 500 x g, then 60 sec at 17,900 x g.

steps.title: Measure DNA Concentration
steps.instruction: Quantify the purified cDNA using a Nanodrop2000.

substeps.instruction: Vortex purified WTA samples briefly and centrifuge.
Set Nanodrop2000 to 'Nucleic Acid' and 'DNA' programs.
Blank the instrument using 1 μl of the same PCR-H2O used for elution.
Measure 1 μl of each sample, cleaning the arm between measurements.
Store purified cDNA at -20°C.
